### 8–16s — B03-DIAGRAM-1
Voiceover: 01 · ELICIT — What happened before “I just knew”?. Reconstruct the comparison set, sensory cue, memory, technical constraint, cultural reference, commercial condition, and rejected alternative. Record uncertainty and the contributor who supplied each part of the judgment.

Treatment: vertical reveal with source footer

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 16–24s — B03-DIAGRAM-2
Voiceover: 02 · DEMONSTRATE — Can the judgment be shown in context?. Pair expert demonstration with a learner attempt, correction, second attempt, and commentary on acceptable variation. Some knowledge is tactile, temporal, embodied, confidential, or culturally governed; not everything belongs on camera.

Treatment: slow evidence push; no synthetic parallax

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 24–32s — B03-DIAGRAM-3
Voiceover: 03 · CONTEST — Who can say the founder is wrong?. Create a review ritual where pattern, textile, production, wearer, commercial, cultural, accessibility, and archive perspectives can challenge a choice. Preserve the reason for override rather than manufacturing consensus.

Treatment: vertical reveal with source footer

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 32–40s — B03-DIAGRAM-4
Voiceover: 04 · GOVERN — Who may retain and teach it?. Attach consent, compensation, attribution, confidentiality, access, teaching, archive, withdrawal, and cultural-authority fields. Keep protected expression, contract rights, trade secrets, know-how, and abstract taste as separate questions.

Treatment: slow evidence push; no synthetic parallax

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
